title: Ports Are Scaling AI. Here’s How to Make It Deliver.
gist: A BCG/TIC4.0 survey of 103 port and terminal leaders (August 2026) finds 44% are scaling AI or beyond but only 4% can tie it to earnings, with unclear ROI (41%) the top barrier and doubt concentrated below the C-suite. Customers (freight forwarders, 3PLs, liners) pull demand, yet benefits stay operational; expected value is shifting from platform building to forecasting, dispatch and workflow integration.

insights.claim: In a 2026 BCG/TIC4.0 survey of 103 port and terminal leaders, 44% have moved beyond early testing into scaling AI or later stages, yet only 4% have embedded AI in core operations and can point to a measurable earnings gain.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Port AI spend is running far ahead of demonstrated P&L impact, so vendor revenue may outpace operator returns.
insights.quote: Nearly 44% of respondents are scaling AI or beyond, yet only 4% can tie it to earnings.
insights.locator: AI adoption is widespread, but earnings impact

insights.claim: Only 11% of surveyed port and terminal respondents systematically track what AI contributes to efficiency or margin.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Operator claims about AI-driven margin improvement are largely unmeasured and should be discounted.
insights.quote: Only 11% of respondents track what AI contributes to efficiency or margin in any systematic way
insights.locator: Activity, however, does not always create value

insights.claim: Scale correlates with AI maturity in ports: 56% of companies with more than $8 billion in revenue report scaling AI or beyond, versus 32% of those below $1 billion.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Large global terminal operators may widen their operational lead over smaller and bulk-port competitors.
insights.quote: 56% reported scaling or beyond, versus 32% of those below $1 billion
insights.locator: Adoption Is Broad, but Proof Is Rare

insights.claim: On average, surveyed port leaders are using or exploring 16 of 43 assessed AI use cases, led by extracting data from shipping documents (62%) and predicting crane or straddle carrier failure (48%).
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Document AI and predictive maintenance are the most penetrated port use cases, indicating where vendor competition is already crowded.
insights.quote: from extracting data from shipping documents (62%) to predicting when a crane or straddle carrier will fail (48%)
insights.locator: To assess how far the industry has come

insights.claim: Many port functions still run on clipboards, radio calls or planner intuition, most visibly at smaller terminals and bulk ports, which is the frontier AI now reaches.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Low digital baseline at small and bulk terminals implies large untapped efficiency headroom.
insights.quote: many port functions still run on clipboards, radio calls, or the gut instincts of a planner
insights.locator: Ports and terminals are no strangers

themes.theme: ROI doubt and the C-suite vs frontline divide

insights.claim: Unclear return on investment is the most-cited barrier to port AI implementation at 41%, ahead of data quality (32%), systems integration (30%), and executional certainty and implementation cost (28% each).
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The binding constraint on port AI adoption is economic proof, not technology availability.
insights.quote: In short, what holds AI back is doubt about whether it will pay off.
insights.locator: Unclear ROI Is the Main Challenge

insights.claim: Only 21% of C-suite port respondents named unclear ROI as a barrier versus 44% below the C-suite, and 14% of senior leaders cited implementation cost versus 30% of others.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Executive AI optimism is not shared by the managers who execute, signaling rollout stall risk.
insights.quote: Only 21% of C-suite respondents named unclear ROI as a barrier, but below the C-suite, the figure jumped to 44%.
insights.locator: That doubt is not spread evenly

insights.claim: Because budgets are approved at the top and pilots run below, AI pilots in ports only scale where executives and frontline managers agree, and stall when the manager closest to the work doubts the payoff.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Top-down AI announcements are weak signals of scaled deployment; frontline buy-in determines realization.
insights.quote: budgets are approved at the top, pilots are run below, and pilots scale only where the two agree
insights.locator: This differentiated point of view on AI

insights.claim: C-suite and non-C-suite port respondents report proven AI value at similar rates (29% vs 26%), suggesting the dispute is over what counts as a credible business case rather than over results.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Standardized ROI definitions could unlock scaling without new technology.
insights.quote: The open question is what counts as a credible business case.
insights.locator: This differentiated point of view on AI

themes.theme: Data, standards, security and talent foundations

insights.claim: Without shared data definitions and semantics, AI can treat superficially comparable port measures as equivalent and draw misleading conclusions, and much port data still sits in fragmented, disconnected systems.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Data standardization is a prerequisite and a potential moat for interoperability providers.
insights.quote: Without shared definitions and semantics, AI can treat two measures that look comparable as if they mean the same thing when they do not
insights.locator: Standardized data quality is the second-most-cited

insights.claim: BCG and TIC4.0's 2025 digital benchmark found most port digital roadmaps are drawn terminal by terminal with no widely adopted standards, even inside multinational terminal groups, and cybersecurity concerns slow cross-organizational planning tools such as berth planning.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Even global terminal operators lack network-level scale benefits from AI, limiting synergy claims.
insights.quote: Most digital roadmaps are still drawn terminal by terminal, with no widely adopted standards
insights.locator: Our 2025 digital benchmark with TIC4.0

insights.claim: Piecemeal, local data fixes in ports tend to move bottlenecks rather than remove them, so enterprise-wide investment in data quality, access and integration unlocks more value than any single AI use case.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Favors operators and vendors pursuing enterprise data platforms over point solutions.
insights.quote: piecemeal fixes tend to move the bottleneck rather than remove it
insights.locator: Fix the foundations enterprise-wide

insights.claim: A quarter of surveyed port respondents plan to join industry collaborations or data-sharing initiatives within two years, with TIC4.0's shared semantics and data models positioned as the landing point.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Emerging port data standards (TIC4.0, PAS 4000, ISO work) could reshape terminal software interoperability.
insights.quote: data that stops at the terminal gate stops creating value there too
insights.locator: A port is a network of various stakeholders

insights.claim: Roughly a quarter of port respondents cite limited in-house AI expertise as a barrier, with smaller shares naming resistance to change and lack of training.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Talent scarcity supports demand for managed AI services and external consultancies in logistics.
insights.quote: The people who can run AI well remain thin on the ground.
insights.locator: Talent is another barrier

insights.claim: Port AI demand is driven by commercial customers rather than regulators: freight forwarders (61%), third-party logistics providers (58%) and container liners (52%) are requesting AI-enabled services, while regulatory orders motivate only 1% of adopters.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Market-led adoption means terminals lagging on AI risk losing share to digitally capable competitors.
insights.quote: this shift is led by the market, not by compliance
insights.locator: Respondents’ own reasons for adopting AI

insights.claim: Cost reduction and efficiency (69%) and competitive pressure (47%) are the main motivations for port AI adoption, and port authorities are a source of demand for 35% of respondents.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Port AI is primarily a cost play, so benefits likely show up in opex before revenue.
insights.locator: Respondents’ own reasons for adopting AI

insights.claim: Port AI benefits are almost entirely operational, with operational efficiency at 74%, faster decision making at 44% and cost reduction at 41%, while better customer experience is cited by only 18%.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Terminals that monetize AI via customer-facing services face an open field and potential pricing power.
insights.quote: Those that turn commercial demand into commercial value will pull ahead of those that keep every gain inside the fence.
insights.locator: Yet the value that respondents report

insights.claim: Ports have previously monetized digital services: vehicle-booking systems since the mid-2000s sharply cut truck turn times and carriers paid booking fees for guaranteed slots; Singapore extended this to vessel slot booking and Antwerp built data exchanges partners turn into services.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Precedent shows ports can charge for digital reliability, suggesting AI-enabled services could become a new fee stream.
insights.quote: carriers proved willing to pay a booking fee for a guaranteed slot
insights.locator: The industry has done this before

themes.theme: Value shifting from building AI to running terminals

insights.claim: Of 36 comparable port AI use cases, respondents named 26 more often as areas of expected future benefit over three years than as areas in use today, 4 unchanged and 6 expected to decline in relevance.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Broad expected expansion of use cases points to sustained port AI spending growth.
insights.quote: The biggest gains foreseen are in running the terminal.
insights.locator: The Payoff Is Shifting from Building AI

insights.claim: Expected benefit from forecasting operational states rises from 49% today to 67%, and integrating AI into daily workflows from 60% to 74%, the most-named use case for future value; real-time dispatch, predictive maintenance and vision-based cargo safety monitoring also advance.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Operational forecasting and dispatch tools are the growth segments for port tech vendors.
insights.quote: integrating AI into daily workflows climbs from 60% to 74%, the most-named use case for future value
insights.locator: Forecasting operational states and their root causes

insights.claim: Customer-facing port AI use cases are expected to grow sharply: answering terminal status queries rises from 25% to 43% and messaging freight forwarders from 39% to 55%.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Customer communication AI in logistics is an emerging opportunity despite low current benefit capture.
insights.locator: Forecasting operational states and their root causes

insights.claim: Expected benefit from internal AI governance falls from 51% to 37% and from internal platform building from 56% to 50%, signaling that the window for winning on platform building alone is closing.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Platform and governance tooling spend in ports may plateau as budgets shift to embedded operational AI.
insights.quote: The window for winning on platform building alone is closing
insights.locator: What recedes is the behind-the-scenes work

insights.claim: In container yards, rule-based systems are giving way to predictive tools such as dwell-time forecasting and smart stacking, which places boxes leaving soonest above those staying longest.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Yard optimization is a concrete AI application with tangible throughput benefits.
insights.quote: so the boxes leaving soonest are not under the ones staying longest
insights.locator: Our digital benchmark traced the same progression

insights.claim: Only 2% of surveyed port respondents report no planned AI spending, with hiring and training AI talent leading at 59%, R&D budgets at 55% and adding AI modules to existing systems at 47%, though the sample leans toward large global players.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Operators are augmenting installed systems rather than replacing them, favoring incumbent terminal software vendors with AI add-ons.
insights.quote: Respondents are buying capability and building on what they already own, rather than replacing it.
insights.locator: The pattern is telling

insights.claim: Half of port respondents expect AI to reshape roles through reskilling or redeployment, 13% expect new roles, and 31% expect lower workforce demand as AI automates processes and decisions.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Labor displacement from port AI could trigger union and community friction affecting rollout pace.
insights.locator: The workforce question runs deeper

insights.claim: Only 14% of C-suite port respondents expect AI-driven head count reduction, versus 34% of respondents at other levels.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Perception gap on job cuts is a labor-relations risk that could slow implementation.
insights.quote: That gap is a reason for leaders to say plainly what they intend.
insights.locator: Here, too, the view depends on seniority

insights.claim: Physical equipment automation at the ship's side and in the yard ranked last among digital capabilities in BCG's benchmark, held back as much by labor agreements and community resistance as by capital cost.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Port automation equipment demand is constrained by labor politics, not just capex budgets.
insights.quote: held back as much by labor agreements and community resistance as by capital cost
insights.locator: The automation in that 31%

themes.theme: Four-move playbook to capture AI value

insights.claim: BCG estimates that 10% of AI value creation comes from algorithms, 20% from technology and data, and 70% from having the right training and processes in place.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: AI winners will be determined by organizational execution rather than model access.
insights.quote: 10% of the value creation comes from algorithms, 20% from technology and data, and 70% from having the right training and processes in place
insights.locator: Four Moves Leaders Can Make

insights.claim: Port leaders should sequence four moves in two stages: first prove value before scaling and fix data foundations enterprise-wide, then shift spending from setup to operations and codevelop commercial upside with customers; operators failing stage one will not get far with stage two.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Provides a checklist to judge whether a terminal operator's AI strategy is credible.
insights.quote: The order matters
insights.locator: Four Moves Leaders Can Make

insights.claim: Every port AI pilot should agree up front on a baseline, expected improvement, timeline and a single outcome owner, with staged rollout, go/no-go gates and the riskiest element tested first.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Disciplined pilot governance is a leading indicator of which operators will convert AI spend into earnings.
insights.quote: Evidence is what wins over a skeptical manager.
insights.locator: Prove value before you scale

insights.claim: Winners of the next phase of port AI will be those focusing on a short list of use cases embedded in core operations and measured against clear outcomes, because connected value compounds while isolated value only accumulates.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Favor operators with focused, measured AI programs over those touting large numbers of pilots.
insights.quote: connected value compounds while isolated value merely accumulates
insights.locator: The Next 12 Months
